literature_notes: Two ledger lines were examined. L1 (PMC8301836) reports a 'PDGFRβ-GFP' fusion expressed in SCCVII cells and sorted by FACS for high GFP signal. The naming convention 'PDGFRβ-GFP' (protein-tag order) unambiguously indicates a C-terminal GFP fusion. The C-terminus of PDGFRB (residue 1106) lies in the intracellular domain (topology 555–1106), so this is an intracellular tag and does not qualify as a surface site. It is recorded in other_positions. L2 (PMC13144515) reports an 'HA-tagged PDGFR-beta' construct generated by 'standard molecular cloning technique' but states no residue, no junction, and no terminus for the HA tag. PDGFRB has one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 33) and one intracellular C-terminus (residue 1106); the topology_derived rule would apply only if the clip established which terminus carries the tag, but it does not. Because the tag position is entirely unstated, this clip cannot ground any site — extracellular or otherwise. No ledger line supports a tolerated insertion on the extracellular face of PDGFRB; zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: PDGFRβ-GFP C-terminal fusion expressed in SCCVII cells; GFP is at the intracellular C-terminus (topology 555–1106), not on the extracellular surface.
